target.title: fix: stabilize embedded prompt caching and native Responses continuation
target.body:
Related: #102175

## What Problem This Solves

Long-lived embedded sessions could lose prompt-cache continuity in three connected ways:

- ambient `room_event` turns changed cache-visible delivery instructions and owner-only tool schemas;
- queued work and preflight, manual, queued, or direct compaction rebuilt prompt/tool state from the current turn's effective delivery mode instead of the session-stable prompt mode;
- the built-in authenticated session stream was mistaken for a custom stream, so `openai-chatgpt-responses` runs bypassed OpenClaw's native cached WebSocket continuation path and replayed full context over managed SSE.

## Fix

- Separate effective source delivery from the session-stable prompt-facing mode. Room events still require `message_tool_only` delivery without rewriting the cached prompt contract.
- Construct executable Pi and Codex `message` tools with the real turn mode, preserving the internal source-reply sink and best-effort behavior; use the stable mode only for model-visible prompt/tool shape.
- Keep one safe room-event owner-only core-tool inventory across sender changes while preserving runtime authorization.
- Carry the prompt-facing mode through primary runs, queued followups, memory flushes, Codex app-server prompt/tool builders, and every compaction entry point.
- Keep Codex reusable thread instructions stable and add strict room-event delivery guidance only to the current turn.
- Mark OpenClaw's built-in session auth wrapper and allow only that known wrapper to select native `openai-chatgpt-responses` continuation. Unmarked custom/provider streams retain their existing routing.

The native route selection is API-based, so it covers GPT-5.5 and GPT-5.6 without model-version branches.

## Evidence

Redacted same-session traces from the reported Discord flow showed tool inventory flipping between 44 and 47 tools and cache reads collapsing to roughly 2k-10k or ceilinging around 37k-40k. With stable prompt/tool shape installed, warm turns reached roughly 49k-52k cached tokens on approximately 51k-55k context.

Behavioral coverage also proves:

- a targetless room-event `message(action=send)` still lands in the internal source-reply sink as `message_tool_only`;
- a two-turn GPT-5.6 Sol WebSocket run sends the second turn with `previous_response_id` and delta-only input instead of replaying full context;
- all supported compaction entry points rebuild from the stable prompt-facing mode.

## Validation

Validated at head `f0d85b0829d54ec9f3bda3406168f8bf2d8c0d6d` on upstream `main` `8dedb0ebcaef2bbe6dcd7b9ad137554b62ac1d21`:

- focused regression suite: 25 project test files, 1,211 tests passed;
- 219 focused Codex/source-delivery tests passed after the final review fixes;
- `pnpm tsgo:prod`, `pnpm check:test-types`, `pnpm tsgo:test:packages`, and the 120-plugin extension package boundary compile passed;
- changed TypeScript passed `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint`; generated prompt snapshots are current;
- all GitHub checks pass, including Real Behavior Proof;
- the exact head is installed locally with gateway RPC healthy and HTTP 200.

## Compatibility And Boundaries

- Effective room-event delivery remains strict; private final text does not become visible.
- Ambient `room_event` turns intentionally use the safe non-owner owner-only core-tool inventory for every sender so their prompt/tool contract stays cache-stable. Owner-only tools such as `cron`, `gateway`, `nodes`, and `computer` are therefore not prompt-visible on those ambient turns.
- Runtime authorization remains enforced; non-owner execution of owner-only tools is still blocked.
- Custom provider/session streams are not rerouted.
- Native `auto` transport may still fall back to SSE after a real WebSocket failure; this change makes native continuation reachable and tested, but does not claim every upstream request will be cached.

The remaining merge decision is whether maintainers accept the cache-stable safe inventory for ambient room events. ClawSweeper found no contributor-facing line-level blocker.

Disclaimer: This PR was filed and updated autonomously by Codex on behalf of the reporter. Private user, channel, host, credential, and full trace identifiers were removed from the evidence.
